title: GreenCup Pilot · Visual Rehearsal Manual
subtitle: Fictional sample deck demonstrating slide-by-slide visual sync, timeline recap, and contradiction guardrails

overview.heading: 4-Week Campus Pilot Recap & Presentation Arc
overview.timeline_title: Pilot Story at a Glance (4 Weeks, 340 Cup Loans)

timeline.body: Two campus cafes launched reusable cups with a **$2 refundable deposit** and a 50¢ first-refill discount. Launch week hit a **90% 48-hour return rate**.
timeline.quote: Flyer claim: '90% of cups come right back!'

timeline.body: Only **one return bin** existed at North Hub—450m from Lecture Block B. Lunch-rush QR scans jammed, pulling weekly returns down to **68%**.
timeline.quote: 42 exit interviews: 'Too far to walk back after class.'

timeline.body: Data showed **distance and scan friction** outweighed the $2 deposit. Phase 2 adds **3 hallway RFID drop bins** and an instant **$4** tap refund.
timeline.quote: Outcome: 68% W4 plateau (109 cups unreturned out of 340).

speakers.title: Part A · Alex Chen · Slides 1–2 (~1m45s)
speakers.desc: **Setup & early traction.** Introduces the 340-cup pilot, deposit pricing, and the Week 1 vs. Week 3 drop-off curve.
speakers.warn: ⚠ Slide 2 alert: Do NOT present the 90% Week 1 headline as the full pilot result—state the 68% plateau upfront.

speakers.title: ★ Part B · Sam Rivera (You) · Slides 3–4 (~2m00s)
speakers.desc: **Diagnosis → Redesign → Takeaways.** Explains why distance beat the $2 deposit, pitches 3 RFID bins, and leads Q&A.

slides.speaker: Alex
slides.title: GreenCup: Campus Reusable Cup Pilot
slides.logic: Opens with scope, scale (340 cup loans across 2 cafes), and clear division of labor between Alex (setup & trend) and Sam (friction analysis & redesign).
slides.guard: State clearly that 68% is the Week 4 stabilized return rate across all 340 loans, avoiding cherry-picked Week 1 numbers.
slides.script: Hello everyone. We are Group Alpha—Alex Chen and Sam Rivera. Over the past four weeks, we ran the **GreenCup reusable cup pilot** across two campus cafes, logging **340 total cup loans**. I will walk through our setup and early adoption curve, and Sam will diagnose why returns dropped and present our Phase 2 redesign.

slides.speaker: Alex
slides.title: Early Traction vs. Week 3 Drop-Off
slides.logic: Contrasts the Week 1 promotional headline (90%) with actual Weeks 1–4 scan logs (79% → 68%), creating tension that sets up Sam's friction diagnosis.
slides.guard: Watchout: Slide 2 displays '90% Return Rate!' in big green text on the left, while the footnote shows 68% by Week 3. Verbally call out that 90% was Week 1 only.
slides.script: In Week 1, our $2 deposit and 50-cent refill discount produced an exciting **90% return rate**. However, **that 90% headline was Week 1 only**. As the full four-week tracker on the right shows, returns fell to 79% in Week 2 and plateaued at **68% in Weeks 3 and 4**—leaving 109 cups unreturned. Next, Sam will explain why our initial design stalled.

slides.speaker: Sam
slides.title: Why Convenience Outweighed the $2 Deposit
slides.logic: Picks up directly from Alex's 68% plateau: pairs two behavioral bottlenecks (450m return walk + slow QR scan) with three concrete fixes for Phase 2.
slides.guard: Keep causal claims bounded: 42 exit interviews indicate distance and queue friction were top complaints, though deposit size and bin placement were not A/B tested separately.
slides.script: Thanks, Alex. Looking at sensor logs and 42 exit interviews, **convenience outweighed the $2 deposit**. First, our single return bin sat 450 meters away at North Hub, far from Lecture Block B. Second, manual QR scans jammed during the 12:15 lunch rush. For Phase 2, we propose **three targeted fixes**: adding **three hallway bins** near lecture exits, switching to **two-second RFID tap-and-drop**, and raising the refundable deposit to **$4** with automatic wallet refunds.
slides.source: Fictional sensor timestamps & 42 student exit interviews

slides.speaker: Sam
slides.title: Key Takeaways & Next Semester Rollout
slides.logic: Synthesizes the pilot into three repeatable behavioral design principles and hands cleanly into Q&A with transparent role split.
slides.guard: Do not read the Q&A footer bullet-by-bullet; invite questions naturally after the third takeaway.
slides.script: To conclude, **three practical takeaways** from our pilot. First, **measure retention over at least four weeks**, not Week 1 launch hype. Second, **place return points where people exit**, rather than forcing a trip back to the cafe. Third, **automate deposit refunds** so returning a cup takes under two seconds. Thank you for listening—we welcome your questions.
